speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I am Dr. Agent; to begin my assessment of your newborn's generalized rash, can you tell me exactly how long the rash has been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Since the rash appeared only one day after birth in a term infant, is there any associated fever, poor feeding, or signs of bleeding like bruising? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and Coagulation Panel.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The description of an erythematous maculopapular rash with pustules on the trunk and extremities, specifically sparing the palms and soles, in a 4-day-old newborn is highly suggestive of Neonatal Herpes Simplex Virus infection or a bacterial sepsis presentation. I will need to see the skin lesions to confirm the morphology.

REQUEST IMAGES: Rash_close_up
REQUEST TEST: HSV PCR (blood, CSF, and lesion swab) & Blood Culture

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HSV PCR (blood, CSF, and lesion swab) - Positive; Blood Culture - Positive

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Herpes Simplex Virus Infection (disseminated) with secondary bacterial sepsis.
